description: We are young innovators passionate about space exploration, technology and STEM education. Our project, LunaQuest Junior, helps children explore life on the Moon through interactive missions and resource management. Our interests include programming, engineering, game design and science education. We welcome team members skilled in software development, UI/UX design, animation, lunar science and storytelling who want to make space learning accessible and exciting for young people.
summary:
LunaQuest Junior is an interactive educational game designed to introduce young learners to the challenges of living and working on the Moon. Developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge, the game places players in the role of a junior astronaut responsible for making decisions during a lunar mission.

Players learn about managing essential resources, planning activities and responding to the difficulties of operating in a lunar environment. Through interactive missions, they explore why oxygen, energy, water and careful planning are important for astronauts working away from Earth.

Instead of learning about space exploration only through reading, children can experiment with decisions and observe their consequences in a simulated mission.

LunaQuest Junior aims to make space science accessible, engaging and understandable for young people, particularly those who may have limited opportunities to experience practical space education. The project encourages curiosity, problem-solving and an interest in science, technology, engineering and mathematics.
details:
LunaQuest Junior: Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer

About the Project

LunaQuest Junior is an educational lunar mission simulation game that introduces children and young learners to the challenges of establishing and maintaining a human presence on the Moon.

The project was developed to make space exploration more practical and engaging, especially for students learning science and engineering.

How the Game Works

Players take responsibility for a simulated lunar mission. They select a mission location, plan their resources and make decisions that affect the survival of their crew.

The game includes two lunar environments: the Equatorial Mare and the South Polar Region.

Players manage essential resources such as oxygen, water, food and power. They also make decisions about habitat protection, technology upgrades and responses to unexpected mission events.

The simulation runs through a 14-day mission. A live dashboard shows how decisions affect the mission, while the final report helps players understand their performance and what they could improve.

NASA Resources and Scientific Learning

LunaQuest Junior draws on NASA educational and scientific resources about the Moon, including information on lunar gravity, surface conditions, exploration and the challenges of sustaining human activity beyond Earth.

The game uses simplified simulation rules for educational purposes. Its resource consumption figures and mission outcomes are not presented as actual NASA mission predictions.

Benefits

LunaQuest Junior helps students understand the importance of planning, resource conservation and engineering decisions in space exploration.

It encourages problem-solving, scientific curiosity and an interest in space-related careers.

The game can also support science clubs and classroom activities, including schools where access to practical space education is limited.

What Makes It Creative

Rather than presenting facts about the Moon as a conventional lesson, LunaQuest Junior allows students to learn through decisions.

Players can experiment with different mission strategies, experience the consequences of resource shortages and discover why astronauts must carefully manage the systems that support human life.

The combination of lunar environments, resource management, mission events and performance feedback creates an interactive learning experience.

Intended Impact

Our goal is to make lunar exploration understandable and interesting to young learners, including students in Uganda.

Through accessible educational games, we hope to encourage more children to explore science, technology, engineering and mathematics.

LunaQuest Junior provides a starting point for learning how engineering, teamwork and scientific knowledge contribute to successful space missions.
